 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh
 On The 9 th Of December, 2024
 Misc. Appeal No. 7150 of 2023
 Pratap Damor And Others
 Versus
Dashrath Singh Rathor And Others
Appearance:
Shri Sachin Parmar - advocate for the petitioners.

Shri Sudhir Dandwate - Advocate for the respondent No.3
 Order

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 03.08.2023 in MACC No.111/2022 by MACT Judge, Ratlam for enhancement of Rs.12 lakhs compensation with interest @ 18% per annum.

2. Facts in brief are that a claim under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act was preferred seeking compensation of Rs.55,50,000/- for the death of Dinesh aged 35 years and working as Labour in a motor accident on 31.03.2022 at 11.30 P.M near Shivgarh, Baajna road, Khriyapada, Ratlam by negligent driving of driver of the Bus bearing No.MP-43P0554 by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured by respondent no.3.
3.
The Claim Tribunal calculated a total compensation of Rs. 10,59,600/- and deducted 25% for contributory negligence and ordered to be satisfying a total compensation of Rs. 7,94,700/-.

4. The loss of dependency was calculated assessing the income of the deceased Rs. 5,500/- per month adding 40% for future prospects and deducted NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:34915 2 MA-7150-2023 1/3rd for personal expenses after applying the multiplier of 16 and also awarded Rs.44,000/- for loss of consortium to all the claimants and Rs. 30,000/- for funeral expenses and loss of estate.
5.
This appeal has been preferred on the ground that income has been assessed on the lower side even the minimum wages has not been taken into consideration.
Loss of consortium and conventional heads have not been properly awarded.
The contributory negligence have not been fastened on the deceased.

sentences.text: 6. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
7. The counsel for the respondent Insurance Company has supported the award.
8. Tribunal ought to have considered Rs. 8,800/- per month as wages payable to the un-skilled labourers on the date of accident.
Accordingly, loss of dependency comes to Rs. 15,77,088/-.
The findings of contributory negligence are proper.

Accordingly, total loss of dependency comes to Rs.
15,77,088/-.

The amount of consortium ought to have been granted to three of the claimants, which ought to have been Rs. 1,32,000/- and in the head of loss of conventional heads it ought to have been awarded Rs. 1339551/-.

9. In view of the above , the compensation is recalculated as under:-
Income Rs. 8,800/-per month + Rs. 3520/-
Loss of Dependency (40% F.P.) = 12,320 x 12 -1/3 x16 =Rs. 15,77,088/-
 Consortium Rs. 1,32,000/ (each appellant 44,000/
 Funeral Rs. 16,500/-
Loss of estate Rs. 16500/-
Total amount Rs. 17,86068  MACT Award Rs. 10,59,600
Enhance amount Rs. 6,86,468  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:34915  3  10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.17,86068/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.10,59,600/-.

Accordingly,
the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.6,86,468/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
11. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.6,86,468/-.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
